claims.text: Depressive symptoms among U.S. adolescents in grades 8 through 12 increased between 2010 and 2015, especially among females.
Suicide-related outcomes among U.S. adolescents in grades 8 through 12 increased between 2010 and 2015, especially among females.
Suicide rates among U.S. adolescents aged 13 to 18 increased between 2010 and 2015.
Adolescents who spent more time on new media were more likely to report mental health issues.
Adolescents who spent more time on nonscreen activities were less likely to report mental health issues.
Since 2010, adolescents spent more time on new media screen activities and less time on nonscreen activities.
Cyclical economic factors such as unemployment and the Dow Jones Index were not linked to adolescent depressive symptoms or suicide rates when matched by year.

evidence.description: Analysis of two nationally representative surveys of U.S. adolescents in grades 8 through 12 (N = 506,820) showed an increase in depressive symptoms between 2010 and 2015, particularly for females.
Analysis of two nationally representative surveys of U.S. adolescents (N = 506,820) showed an increase in suicide-related outcomes between 2010 and 2015, particularly for females.
National statistics on suicide deaths for individuals aged 13 to 18 indicated increased suicide rates between 2010 and 2015.
Survey data indicated that adolescents spending more time on electronic devices and social media were more likely to report mental health issues.
Survey data showed lower likelihood of mental health issues among adolescents engaging in in-person social interaction, sports, homework, print media, and religious services.
Survey trends after 2010 demonstrated a shift toward increased screen time and decreased nonscreen time among iGen adolescents.
Year-matched economic indicators, specifically unemployment rate and the Dow Jones Index, demonstrated no link to depressive symptoms or suicide rates.

methodologies.name: Cross-temporal survey and statistical trend analysis
methodologies.description: Analysis of trends across two nationally representative adolescent surveys, national mortality statistics, and macroeconomic indicators matched by year.
datasets: Two nationally representative surveys of U.S. adolescents in grades 8-12 (N = 506,820)
U.S. national statistics on suicide deaths (ages 13-18)
conditions: Year-matched economic indicators (unemployment, Dow Jones Index)
